title: The Fall of Constantinople: The Siege that Ended an Empire
character: weathered 49-year-old Byzantine Emperor Constantine XI Palaiologos with dark greying beard, wearing gilded Roman lamellar cuirass and imperial purple paludamentum cloak
sources: Sphrantzes, Georgios, The Fall of the Byzantine Empire
Critobulus of Imbros, History of Mehmed the Conqueror
Niccolo Barbaro, Diary of the Siege of Constantinople (1453)
Steven Runciman, The Fall of Constantinople 1453 (1965)

lines.text: For over one thousand years, these colossal stone walls were invincible—until one morning in 1453.
lines.visual: colossal triple Theodosian Walls of Constantinople at night, towering stone bastions and deep moats, Ottoman siege trenches and burning fires stretching to the horizon, dark misty dusk, 35mm film

lines.text: Sultan Mehmed the Second unleashed the greatest super-weapon of the Middle Ages: a bronze cannon firing twelve-hundred-pound boulders.
lines.visual: massive Ottoman bronze super-cannon the Basilisk firing on the battlefield, enormous flash of orange fire and black gunpowder smoke, stone masonry crumbling from the ramparts

lines.text: When Roman chains blocked the harbor, seventy Ottoman warships were dragged entirely overland on greased logs.
lines.visual: hundreds of Ottoman soldiers and oxen dragging large wooden war galleys over steep wooded hills on greased timber rollers under torchlight, naval fleet moving across land

lines.text: On May twenty-ninth, thousands of elite Janissaries stormed the fractured Saint Romanus gate.
lines.visual: chaotic breach in the stone walls, waves of Janissaries in white felt caps charging with curved kilij swords and polearms through choking smoke and boiling Greek fire

lines.text: Refusing to flee, Emperor Constantine the Eleventh tore off his imperial insignia and charged into the breach.
lines.visual: dramatic close-up of Emperor Constantine XI in battle-scarred gilded Roman lamellar armor, drawing his sword with intense determination, smoke swirling around his face

lines.text: The Roman Empire finally fell where its last emperor stood. Subscribe to Beyond History for more epic battles.
lines.visual: majestic cinematic dawn shot of Hagia Sophia cathedral rising above the misty Golden Horn as dawn sunlight breaks through clouds, epic documentary pull-back
